translation: To Imdī-ilum from Uzua: After I arrived in Kunanamit, and I was far from your breast, may Aššur and Ištar-zat witness that becasue I never recevied heard any of your letters, I set out towards you. I said to myself, " .. so that I may see the eye of my father and lord." I came down and I gatehred togethre every shekel of silver. Because I had not heard any of your messages whatsoever, I made my way to the kārum-office. I am protective of your reputation and wherver I gave a talent for putchases, I am able to raise a 10 shekels rate in silver. And I have done many favors Also, I myself here to every shekels of silver which I made I hwl'd And i will z'b. My dear father and lord, who but I is your true servant I will lose from ... Also, for years I will make every shekel of silver. When I heard your tablet and Abu-šalim spoke the instructions which you ..., I sent these tablets five time to you so taht you would not return the instructions. If you desire, you will indeed approach to your breast and I will see your eye. The packer of Pūšu-kēn which you cleared from being a sāridum hauler, let me set another name before you. The package worth 10 minas silver, when you sold it on credit to the merchant, give the package worth 10 mians silver and mine so thatI can give from the top of the package which you sold, 10 talents washed copper from Durḫumit to your representative and I will casue the copper to arrive at Purušḫattum and I wil send the silver as much as it fetches to the city and they may make purchases for my package from your house. Apart from these matters, make amends with me and I every shekel of silver which is in your possession when I see as soon as you are deducted, this 'nabritum'' in Kunanamit I will bru it to you your qiptum and whatever I make I will see. Why is that, with regard to your tablet concerning the transport of Abu-šalim, which I heardread, 5 talents washed copper toa reliable merchant who is after her every talent of copper which they will weigh out I gave to you concerning this ... I ate. If these words should have been evil, I would depart for you. Indeed, let Ištar-pilaḫ hear so that until he is released there I will not klm my bulatia to you. After he left, 10 talents washed copper I opened for you. 15 talents washed copper I will send to you. Now let him ... you my debt and sell my goods. And when I see your eye ..... Truly, I am not your servant Let Ištar-pilaḫ come with your young manson, so that I may depart and see your eye. Why should your eye ... I keep asking. I hear that my maḫāúm left with Amur-Ištar. Dispatch him with Ištar-pilaḫ. The son of Puzur-... ,,,, Let your message come to the city, to Puzur-Mus and our ladies.

translation: Elāya and Aššur-mālik owe Puzur-Aššur 1 mina silver. They will pay 7 weeks from the ḫamuštum of Puzur-Aššur. If they do not pay on time, they will add interest at a rate of 1 12 shekels per month Month: Teʾintātim. Eponymate: Aššur-imittī the boatman. The obligation to pay back the silver is bound to whichever one is financially solvent and legally responsible. Witnesses: Ikuppiya, Zuzubar.

translation: Ikūnim owes Aššur-imittī 23 12 minas 3 shekels refined silver. He will pay 40 weeks from the ḫamuštum of Amurrum-bāni and Ikūnim. If he does not pay at the fulfillment of his term, he will add interest at the rate of 1 12 shekels per mina per month. Month: Allānātim Eponymate: Sukkallīya Witnesses: Aššur-rēʾī, Azunāya, Aššur-mālik.

If he does not pay then, he will add 1½ shekels per mina as interest according to colony policy. Eponymate: Aššur-damiq. Witnesses: Kiliya, Puzur-Ištar

translation: From Elamma to Aššur-nādā, Iddin-abum and Aššur-lamassā: specifically to Aššur-lamassī: My tin which you brought up here from the City, send me word about where you entrusted it on commission; also, write the names of your witnesses in the letter. Then you yourself should write a note about your witnesses, with their names, so that when they convene you can there remind those to whom you entrusted goods about the names of your witnesses. Send me word about who was not and who was present.

translation: To Aššur-nādā from Ša-ša-aḫ-šu-šar: Since you had left they have received 23 mina 5 shekels of silver and given that to Uṣur-ša-Aššur son of Aššur-malik. Uṣur-ša-Aššur has taken 3 kutānu-textiles and deposited them in the port office. They received 12 shekels of silver from Šarapunuwa and gave that to me. The house of Kutubiš brought 4 sacks of barley; I received it here and 1 12 sack will be for myself. The house of Ka'uba brought 3 sacks of wheat. However, they did not give me anything. 15 shekels of silver from Tarhunu, they owe the rest of the silver; thereof they have given me 8 14 shekels of silver. However, they did not give me anything else, and 5 shekels remain owed by Tarhunu. Also, it was they who took the rest of the silver. They have received nothing from your outstanding claims. Make Uṣur-ša-Aššur pay attention to your orders. The term for repayment is overdue by three months. Even firewood he did not buy for me, so I myself have bought it. From Habi we have received 1 23 mina 5 shekels of silver; Uṣur-ša-Aššur has taken it. 23 mina we got from Haluli; also, Uṣur-ša-Aššur has received 5 shekels of silver.

translation: To Ikuppia, Ennam-Aššur and Sumi Abiya from Aššur-Nada; to Ennam-Aššur and Sumi-Abiya: I entrusted to you 16 half-packs of each 1 talent and 7 top-packs of 30 minas, apart from those belonging to Puzur-Ištar, plus 6 black donkeys. Thereof I sent with you 1 talent 25 minas of copper, that 1 received from Úsur-ša-Aššur, to Ikuppia. 1 talent 12 minas of copper belonging to Ennam-Aššur; 1 talent 20 minas which I balanced with you on behalf of Puzur-Ištar--- the rest of the copper: 15 12 talents 3 minas. Thereof 5 12 talents 3 minas of copper belong to the tamkārum. When the sale has been carried out the tamkārum will pay me 15 112 talents. And the one who resolved my dispute was Ennam-Aššur, so do not seize anycopper, and without any authorisation the tamkārum must not appropriate the 15 12 talents ofcopper for which I hold a certified tablet, lest you let it get out of my reach. As for the rest of the copper, 10 talents from Kunanamit plus the 6 donkeys, I said: "Come, I shall pay you"-so I trusted you, but you cheated me, saying: "I shall lay claim to the 10 talents of copper and the 6 donkeys, turn that into copper of good quality in Durhumit, bring it to Kaneš and your representatives will pay me in full in silver." I did not payout the copper and the donkeys to you. Why did you then say: "I have been paid." The donkeys belong to Ikuppia Release the donkeys to him For the rest of your silver I shall personally guarantee for you. may Aššur and Amurrum, the gods of our fathers, know: on top of the fact that I guaranteed for your joint-stock capital, it was no stranger who denounced me It is you who keep denouncing me in colony after colony

translation: Buṣānim owes Adad-ṣulūlī 1 mina 15 shekels refined silver. He will pay 24 weeks from ḫamuštum of Innāya and Aššur-mālik, month of Kuzalli, eponymate of Aššur-idī. If he does not pay, he will add 1 12 shekel per mina per month.

translation: As for the activities of shipping, when your instructions come with the ṣuharū-servants of Pūšu-kēn, in your tablet it said, "Send 12 minas silver from Ea-šār." For those, both to the man and yours about 10 minas silver which I caused to be siezed, I did not send it late. I said, "Let aboundant silver arrive and let him be happy." When I was in Waḫšušana, Ṭāb-ṣilla-Aššur received 8 13 minas tin from the goods of the merchant. He said, "I took it for the price of the donkeys which they took for Dān-Aššur." I said, "Deduct 23 mina silver as the price of your donkey. Give back the rest." He said, "He took my donkeys for 50 shekels silver" I said, "Leave it. One could assist your donkey ." He did not see things my way. There, let him clear for the 8 minas 50 shekels tin. As for the 20 shekels silver which Ismanum owes to you, I gathered 20 shekels silver from my own funds and Ṭāb-ṣilla-Aššur paid his son. 20 shekels silver for the hire of Ṭāb-ṣilla-Aššur in his first transport, he said, "I will purchase tin for you at a 17 shekel rate."

Kuṣiya said to Dān-Aššur, "My dear brother, the three minas silver which you gave to the son of Erraya in our matter and which went to the city and which the son of Erraya consumed the profit of the silver and you took your share, give me the silver so that I can divide it to the son of Erraya. Also, add add about a mina of silver to this silver so that I can pay off our matter with Kudādum." We ... translation: From Šalim-aḫum to Ennam-Aššur: As for your outstanding claims with both the Anatolians and wherever, which I continue to hear about, clear yourself before the caravan from Ḫaḫḫum arrives. In addition to the silver which you sent to me with Innaya, send as much silver as you can lay your hands on ahead of you as an installment. Come home Do not leave my assets behind, i.e. the silver from the tin in the caravan of Aššur-mālik s. Luzina. Send the silver from Šāt-Aššur's and Azia's tin ahead of you. Now, do not mix the proceeds of their textiles with that of my goods Bring 15 minas of top-quality fine copper from both Kanesh and Ḫaḫḫum. I shall give you the 16 12 shekels gold owed you by Li--en in Šimala. Bring a tabletop one and half cubits in size. There are legs available here. Let Agua s. Tāb-Aššur give to you the table which he owes me.

translation: From Šalim-aḫum to Pūšu-kēn and Dān-Aššur: On the day that you read this tablet, send the 20 minas silver and its interest about which you wrote with the first departure. Also, dispatch Ḫanu. Let Dān-Aššur spend the nabrītum and in addition ot the silver from the transport of Ḫuraṣānum and the 7 12 minas silver from my textiles in the transport of the son of Aššur-mālik about which you wrote, add the proceeds of the tin and the textiles from the transport of Dān-Aššur and that from his donkeys, and that from my outstanding claims, the taḫšištum that I gave to you here,and send in total 1 talent silver with Dān-Aššur. As for the 55 textile from the transport of the son of Errāya, why is it that I have written you 30 times As for my share of the textiles, gather the silver in addition to that from the transport of Ḫuraṣānum. As for the merchandise both from the transport of Dān-Ašsur and from that which I am now sending you with the caravan, clear my tin and textiles so that Dān-Aššur can bring eveyr single shekel of silver that you placed on merchants, the cleared amount, in his transport. Concerning the matter of Dān-Aššur, send silverof your own funds, as much as you can send, and I myself will put down two shares so that I purchase for whatever price you write, so that Dān-Aššur my bring it to you in the first caravan. In addition to the 6 shekels gold from Panaka and the yield of the textiles which the boy gave to you you add as much gold as you can so that the merchant send the pašallum gold. Let Dān-Aššur bring the 40 minas of fine copper.

translation: From Šalim-aḫum to Pūšu-kēn: To Dān-Aššur: You wrote me. You said, "45 minas silver which the merchant brought to you." translation: To Idī-abum, Aššur-mālik, Aššur-imittī, Šū-Anum, Enna-Suen, and Puzur-ilī, from Pilaḫ-Ištar: The message of the amtum wife has come to me once or twice. Regarding Ilī-nādā s. Baziya, why is it that over there he constantly threatens to distrain my amtum-wife, attempts to seal the house and constantly frightens my people My father was alive ten years ago, during the plague. Why did he not seize my father Or not deposit memoranda to my father Iliš-tikal assembled my father's silver. Why did he not take from my father's silver, or from the attorney or give a memoranda to Iliš-tīkal I and my brothers met five times with him, in Purušḫattum, Ulama, and Waḫšušana Why didn't he give us any memoranda And how is it that his messages never came Nor did he send messages to his representatives with the result that they did not write anything down. Also, his son, Šū-Bēlum, served as caravan driver with me, and he was constantly taking 1 or 2 minas silver in his bundle to him in Ulama and he did not 'ripen' the merchandise in the house of his own father. Why did he not seize from my silver My dear fathers and lords, do you not know that because a robbery occurred when my father died, much silver and my father's tablets were stolen My dear fathers, my brothers opened the strongroom five years ago and since then it has been deposed for a matter. As for my brothers, it is heard they are on the caravans. But here, I myself have released 1 or 2 minas silver each day at the gate of the market and because of this I am thus made to assemble. If Ilī-nādā prosecutes the case there, he will claim everything. My dear fathers and lords, I am the son of a dead man I will come to GN and we will set the matter before the colony so that they will raise the matter to the city and resolve this. Here I will clear myself and will come so that we can open my father's strongroom and inspect the tablets and the memoranda and clear the matter for the man, and those that stood at the head of my father here will search. Becasue that silver is his debt, and we wrote him down for that silver, he will not return it to Kalaluwa for him. A great many of my fathers tablets were stolen

translation: To Šū-Ištar, the priest of Ištar, this is what Aššur-lamassāi, Nimar-Ištar and Adad-rabi said: The day the son of Aplum arrived we chased Aššur-rabi and the daughter of Ihan-il out of your house in accordance with your written order; then, we brought your amtum-wife Watniašwe and your son Aššur-imittī into your house and she is in possession of the attributes of priesthood. Aššur-rabi went to the colony and said: “My father sent me a message to leave the house. Select for me five independent traders so that I can entrust the goddess and her jewellery and leave.” The colony selected five independent traders for him and he entrusted the goddess and her jewellery; she is fine. ... the jewellery of the goddess, be it silver or gold or meteoric iron or sādum gold ... the selected men wrote it on a tablet and gave that to your amtum-wife. A dispute arose among your amtum-wife, Nimar-Ištar, Aššur-imitti and Ewrimuša, who are in possession of your house, and the taboo of the goddess has been heard. They went to the colony and the colony sent the same men as previously selected to take care of the goddess; they checked the jewellery of the goddess with this result: 12 earrings of meteoric iron; 1 1⁄2 shekel ca. 12½ g, a representation of a pudendum of gold; 2 beads of gold of two-thirds of a shekel ca. 5½ g; half a mina ca. 249 g of silver: toggle-pins; 17 stars of silver; a mace of 56 shekels ca. 6.9 g of silver; beads of either sādum gold or lapis lazuli weighing 35 shekels ca. 290½ g, forming the string of beads on her chest all this is lost. The colony cross-examined them and they replied: “Yes, we took it.”

translation: From Šalim-aḫum to Pūšu-kēn and Ilabrat-bāni, specifically to Ilabrat-bāni: From Lā-qēpum's tablet: "Ilabrat-bāni took 6 13 minas tin from your sack and at that time he went to Hattum." Ilī-ašranni brought a white kusītum robe for my votive offering to Aššur-mālik. But Aššur-mālik did not arrive. He had departed. You took the kusītum robe yourself. You said, "It is delivered to my father." You promised 15 shekels silver to Dān-Aššur. You said, "I will send it after you." You have held that one since the year of Aḫ-marši REL 79. My dispatch came to you five times Give Pūšu-kēn the silver for the tin, the kusītum robe, and the half kutānum textile. Or, send so that I can take from your silver here. Aššur-mālik son of Azua brings you three textiles belonging to my votive fund and one textile for the girl with your textiles. Give a mina of silver to Pūšu-kēn so that he puts it in my silver. Are you not constantly hearing that every year, wherever we sell, I must quarrel with groups of five or ten people concerning even a single shekel of your silver May Aššur and Ilabrat witness that whenever I give a single shekel of silver, I am bereft of 10 or 20 minas of my silver. My dear brother, do not anger me Give my silver to Pūšu-kēn. Or send to me so that I may take from your silver here. Do not anger me

translation: From Šalim-aḫum to Lā-qēpum and Pūšu-kēn: My dear brothers, my tin and textiles should not be stocked up. From the silver pertaining to Ḫuraṣānum and Aššur-mālik and the textiles worth 7 12 minas silver about which you wrote, seal 30 minas silver and send it with the first departing travellers. As much silver as he sends or is there from the transport of Kulumaya and Agua, if anything is sold, or of donkeys, wherever there is a single shekels of silver, clear it and dispatch Dān-Aššur here. My dear brother, give heed to my instructions and so make me happy. As for the silver owed by Puzur-Adad and Ennum-Aššur, if their term is up, have them pay. Seal 30 minas silver and send it here. If Dān-Aššur does not bring the maid, I will be very disappointed. In your tablet you said, "Aššuriš-tikal has the silver of Apila." Make him pay the silver.

Sukkalliya stating, "8 minas silver of the 2 minas gold which he took.",inform me as to whether or not the tablet is available. translation: To Aššur-imittī and Šū-Ḫubur from Pūšu-kēn: I wrote 28 minas 48 shekels silver at the colony office. For this silver I both weighed out your silver and sold textiles. translation: Regarding the 54 minas 45 12 shekels silver from the šēpum of Aḫ-šalim which you 'entrusted' on long terms, 58 minas 18 12 shekels from the šēpum of Pūšu-kēn, 28 minas 27 shekels from Lulu son of Zukuḫūm, 31 12 minas which Aššur-šamši and Ḫinnāya 'entrusted' in Durḫumit, 5 minas from Amur-Ištar for my tin, you two wrote me. You said, "Ḫinnāya will pay it, and our message will go to him." Thereof, Šū-Suen and the son of Šū-Aššur brought me 31 minas 15 shekels--its The son of Errāya brought me 20 56 minas--its Dān-Aššur brought me 31 minas 15 shekels--its šadduatum 12 mina-- and 2 minas separately - the corresponding amount to his textiles. Ilī-ālum brought me 41 23 minas--its Kurub-Ištar brought me 18 minas 18 shekels. Total: 147 minas 18 shekels silver which they brought me The remainder of the silver is 30 minas 33 shekels, those whose terms are past Don't listen to the interest. Have the silver paid and send it to me immediately. In your tablet you said, "7 minas 35 23 shekels silver from the shipment of Aḫ-šalim is placed on merchants on 'long' terms. As for the 31 minas 18 12 shekels silver arising from the shipment of Aššur-mutabbil and Nūr-Ištar, if their terms are full, have them pay the silver and send it immediately. As for the silver which Ili-ālim and Kurub-Ištar brought, why has the tablet become too heavy for you to send Don't send that to me.

translation: To Pūšu-kēn from Kulumaya and Kurub-Ištar From Kulumaya As soon as the merchandise of Dān-Aššur ... I spoke to you. I said, "Here are the 6 kutānum-textiles for Šāt-Aššur." The textiles do not belong to Šalim-aḫum's daughter; rather, the textiles belong to Kurub-Ištar. My name is on the fringe of the textiles. Ilabrat-bāni is not informed. They wrote a tablet of the merchant for Dān-Aššur. His textiles, they are those from Kurub-Ištar. To Pūšu-kēn from Kurub-Ištar: My dear father, my dear lord, take heed to give the textiles to Šalim-Aššur. If he does not want to accept them, speak to him before two witnesses and send your message. Also, the textiles which Dān-Aššur owes, are to my name. Send the textiles brought by Qarwiya's packer and the tin of Amur-Aššur son of Sukkalliya.

translation: From Pūšu-kēn, the representatives of Puzur-Aššur, and Sueyya to Puzur-Aššur: We checked the 19 talents of refined copper under seals which Ea-šar brought, and it was deficient 13 23 minas. Thereof, they brought 1 talent 40 minas of poor quality copper from the previous and former washed copper. We checked the 7 12 talents of poor quality copper under seals which Ea-šar brought, and it was deficient 10 minas. All this Ea-šar brought. 3 talents of 'black' copper are placed in his copper. They brought 2 talents of refined copper which he deposited in Walama and we checked it and it was deficient 1 mina. 20 minas of poor quality copper are deposited in the previous caravan-enterprise. We checked the 10 talents 30 minas of poor quality copper under seals which Kurara and Šū-Bēlum brought, and it was deficient 12 minas. Your representatives brought 52 textiles from Waḫšušana. Thereof, 30 kutānum-textiles are deposited to Pūšu-kēn at a rate of 9 14 shekels of silver and he has not yet paid the silver. Idī-Aššur drove here 48 kutānum-textiles. Total of your textiles is 148 textiles which arose from the transport of Idī-Aššur. Enna-Suen son of Elāli is bringing you 20 minas silver under our seals. We will convert to silver the copper, the textiles, and the outstanding claims and assets which you left like gentlemen, and we will clear your silver from the cargo of Dān-Aššur and we will send your silver to you. According to your instructions your donkeys are put to pasture. Your servant is well.

Thereof, 27 fine šurbuitum-textiles, their price 3 minas 21 23 shekels, 63 kutānum-textiles, their price 6 minas 1 13 shekels, total 90 kutnum-textiles, their price 9 minas 23 shekels, then 15 minas 'hand-tin,' their price at 14 shekels per shekel of silver was 1 minas 4 13 shekels, 2 black donkeys, their price 1 mina 14 shekels, 15 shekels silver for their feed, 12 23 shekels for their gear, 21 12 shekels add 'added expenses,' 4 shekels for their head-tax--they levied that on your "servant," 6 shekels the exit tax, 3 23 shekels silver for 'saetum,' 45 shekels from the tithe he 'set.' In addition to the 10 minas previous copper from Iluwa, which is 'on his account,' 15 12 shekels silver we increased to him. As for the 7 13 minas silver which we paid out to Aššur-imittī, 23 minas interest we added. As for the 6 talents of copper which were the price of the houses of Abum-ilī, we added 30 minas copper interest. At a 1 12 mina rate, their price in silver is 4 23 minas. We paid 4 minas 22 56 shekels for the house of Sutiya. We took the tablet of your debt. 56 minas to Tupezi. X shekels for the reeds and hire for Ziarim, 1 textile belonging to Aššur-bāni, 1 textiles belonging to Šalim-Aššur, all this Urani brings to you.

translation: From Aššur-imittī to Pūšu-kēn: I owe you 5 12 minas refined silver here. What is it that you wrote You said, "I withheld silver from your account to your accountings, to your sales." I don't owe money there Indeed You're witholding silver which I owe you here Now, if I do not owe silver there, then weigh out silver from your own funds and let it be a loan from you for a month or two Everything goes to Kurub-Ištar and you have not collected silver from the son of Al-āḫum or from my merchants whose terms are full, and you have not sent it. I anticpated 20 minas or more of silver. You sent only 7 minas. My dear brother, in whom else can I trust there Heed my instructions Wherever there is a single shekel of silver, collect it and send it From my merchandise to my accountings ... my own sharespendable cash. Enter into the house of Aššūr-rēʾī and take my tablets so that they are in your possession. At the very moment of his dying, he said something about my name He took something of my silver there Learn something and send me some good news and thus inform me. Also, his silver of his naruqqum, no one must take anything. Seal it and send it here. Concerning the purchase of the son of Šū-Aššur about which you wrote, "If I do not write you anything in the next 10 days, I will clear you." It is lost.not here. If ..., send so that with you I may be able to šxx.

translation: To Pūšu-kēn from Kuzallim: Say to P I owe 20 minas of silver to Enna-Suen son of Šū-Ištar and I set his share at 15 minas of silver to the city. I owe 20 minas of silver to Enna-Suen son of Šū-Ištar I set his share at 15 minas of silver to the city I dispatched copper worth 20 minas of silver two months ago to Purushattum. translation: To Pūšu-kēn from Amur-Ištar: According to your message, regarding the 43 minas of tin which are brought to you and the 9 kutānum-textiles which you sent from Kaneš, I said, "As for me, the man wrote to me. I did not strike the share." I did my best with about a mina of silver of my own funds and I wrote a tablet which stated '10 minas of refined silver in the presence of Ašina, the affiliated trader' and Šuluma brings it to you under his seal and my seal. My dear father, take care to send my textiles to Purušḫattum. I will take care to clear my own funds and come to you in Kanesh so that at that time you will open the tablets referring to the matters about which I wrote you. Becasue the matters do not 'go out' to justice, I did not inform those matters which were written in your letters. I hold your messages. I gave Šuluma 2 minas of copper for expenses.

translation: To Pūšu-kēn, Puzur-Ištar, Ilabrat-bāni, and Idī-īštar from Tariš-mātum and Bēlātum: We sent the attorney. And the attorney holds a sealed tablet of the city. As for the fact that no one must approach anyone either in the city or abroad, they will divide the silver that Šū-Nunu gathered in the city, here in the city according to their witnesses. They will confiscate every shekel received by anyone who makes claims abroad We are hearing that you are plundering the men for his goods. Also, P You must keep answering the man the mehratim. Urgent, do not addtake away anything from the silver Let them gather the silver to the city and let your representatives take it and wherever there is a single shekels of silver in the city to be sent , let your reports be cleared. To Pūšu-kēn: As for us, we have no father beside you. If you are our father, set witnesses on whomever makes a claim on his silver., so that he does not steal silver from him. Take care to gather the silver and entrust it to the attorney so that he brings it here. Urgent, do not fear Be diligent Also, regarding the textiles, the tithe which you credited, which we gave to the son of Šū-Nunu, take care to send me 3 13 minas silver in good time. Be diligent

translation: To Imdi-ilum and Pūšu-kēn, from Kurūb-Ištar: As for my merchandise in the transport of Imdī-ilum about which you wrote me, you said, "We entrusted what we could. And the remainder, cheap or dear, we will sell and we will send you the silver." My dear brothers, let you full message come as soon as possible regarding what you gave on credit, and what you sold cheap or dear, and as much silver as I have deposited in the colony office. Ameta brings you 2 12 minas exceedingly fine carnelian and a goblet of carnelian under my seal. If the going rate is 6 minas silver or higher, sell the carnelian. If 12 mina pašallum-gold or higher, sell the goblet. If no sales arise, then do not sell. As for the carnelian and the goblet, until I come, its heart and tin prices that will make me a little look for and I will borrow an amount around 10 or 15 minas silver and make a purchase. My brothers either from the previous merchandise or from the price which Ameta brought to you, sell. Seal the silver and let Būr-Suen bring it at the earliest opportunity. If Būr-Suen is not available, give it to the first affiliated trader and let him bring it. If there is not silver from the goods, my dear brothers, give silver from your own funds. .... let it be a loan to you, and let it be a favor to me. To Pūšu-kēn: The one mina carnelian about which you wrote, we received it. Ameta brings your... to you.

translation: From Šalim-aḫum to Pūšu-kēn: Regarding the matter of Ilabrat-bāni about which you wrote, "On the day which I am writing the tablet, his term is full. Purchase cleared tin. Let Dān-Aššur depart with Puzur-Aššur to Amurrum and seize the tin on his own authority." Dān-Aššur was ill and did not go. Ennum-Aššur brings my instructions to you. Now, Puzur-Aššur departed with him and Ennam-Aššur seized the tin on his own authority from lit. in the goods of Ilabrat-bāni’s son, and deposited it with Puzur-Aššur and I received 19 minas 53 56 shekels. Get the remainder of my silver there, 51 16 shekels. Now, wherever he is, write to him the following: Let your message come as to whether he send the remainder of the silver to you or not. 12 minas 15 shekels silver which you sent to me, tin is purchased. Now, I will raise what I can and I will purchase more tin and I will dispatch Dān-Aššur and Puzur-Aššur. As for the 18 fine Send 5 minas silver so that I can make purchases and can cause the goods to reach there while you are still there and maximize profit. My dear brother, besides you in whom can I trust Heed my messages

Combine the tin and textiles and sell them on short or long term credit Wherever the price is even a single shekel higher, sell as much as you are able and make known to me the silver and the terms in your tablets. If there are no merchants as reliable as your surety, do whatever is in my best interests.

translation: From Šalim-aḫum to Pūšu-kēn: Concerning the matter of Ilabrat-bāni, as for the 29 minas of his silver, I weighed out 8 minas silver for a pouring of the son of Al-āḫum. I gave 12 12 minas to his mother, his sister, and his representatives and 17 minas to your representatives about which you wrote. Dān-Aššur will drive to him 1 talent 10 minas tin, 2 textiles, and a black donkey. We paid 5 minas 25 shekels silver for that merchandise. And paid 12 mina for 'additional expenses' of his silver. He requested silver from you for management. Reject him and so that he pays you the remainder of my silver As for my tin and my textiles which you entrusted to him, When it is him he paid the silver. Now, let it be a favor to me Every year I have given him silver, I am embroiled in arguments. Who amoung us here in Aššur have sold him tin on interest and got our silver Now, as for the rest of his silver, there is a tablet or two of a merchant. The hand is indeed quite slack.

translation: To Pūšu-kēn from Dān-Aššur: My dear father and lord, do not treat me harshly. Regarding the copper at the palace, until this day they are putting us off. As for me, an illnes beset me and until now I was stuck here. But I am now well. Don't be overly concerned. I will wait 5 more days, and if the copper of the palace does not come out, I will take my weapon and depart for Purušḫattum.

translation: To Šalim-aḫum from Pūšu-kēn: Aššur-mālik brought 61 textiles, together with the goods of the transporter, and together with the things which you sent to Ilabrat-bāni. Thereof, the excise was 3 kutānum textiles. And you will balance the excise of 1 textile. The purchases was 6 kutānum textiles and they will repay you 3 shekels silver. They cleared 52 kutānum textiles, and you will receive 2 16 shekels. Thereof, Aššur-mālik deposited 1 kutānum textile to your account according to your instructions. Your transporter took 3 of your kutānum textiles and your transporter brings 25 shekels silver its excise added and shipping duty paid. They cleared the remainder of your textiles, 48 textiles. translation: To Pūšu-kēn from Kulumāya: Ikūppīya brought 5 minas silver and 23 minas gold under your seal. Your silver was sold at a rate of 13 shekels silver. Its silver is 4 minas 53 shekels. You wrote. You said, "Kuziziya brings you 15 minas 37 12 shekels silver, its excise added. Weigh it out to the price of the houses of Issu-rīk's son and pull out my tablet and put it among my tablets in the storeroom." Your representatives and Šalim-aḫum opened the package under your seal in front of 5 merchant-class individuals and they took the excise and the cut the remainder of the package and there was 14 minas 37 shekels and 1 minas silver was deducted against your documentation. There, you must not disagree with the weighing. Because Ilabrat-bāni issi'd 1 mina silver as losses, and weighed out 16 minas silver to us, and we set witnesses for us for an amount of 17 minas silver and we took it as 17 minas according to the shipment of Ilabrat-bāni, you wrote. You said, "I will send you 8 minas silver next." When the maatum caravan u-x-x-ni, we received at the house of the merchant the 7 12 minas silver as the equivalent of 8 minas. Altogether, your silver is 33 minas 24x shekels. Thereof, Kulumaya brings 350 kutānum-textiles-they cost 20 12 minas silver,14 donkeys - their cost was 3 minas 14 shekels silver, their feed was 23 mina silver, 1 talent 5 minas hand tin at a rate of 14 shekels - its silver was 4 minas 37 shekels, 5 shekels for sa'itum- 1½ minas capital payment for 3 packers, 6 shekels for their outfitting, 16 12 shekels for the exit tax, 3 shekels losses from the purification, 1 12 shekels for the outfitting of Kulumaya, and 10 12 minas tin separately His silver hire is 45 shekels.

Sell my merchandise wherever it is profitable and send off the silver to me. Now, as for the silver owed by Ememe, why have you not sent it to me until this day Also, clear the son of Ibnili and send me a message. Why is it that Nab-Suen said, “Šū-Kūbum took my silver.” Instead of laying claim in the city, I dropped the matter. Kiliya said to the representatives of Nab-Suen, “If you make a claim, I will go to the city assembly.” Kiliya took the silver. Now, they sealed Saliya’s tablet. I didn’t receive anything.

translation: To Idī-Aššur, Adad-bāni, Aššur-imittī, Ikuppī-Aššur, Puzur-Ištar and Imdī-ilum, from Pūšu-kēn, Puzur-Tiamtum, and Innaya: With regard to the matter of Šū-Aššur about which you wrote, when we read your tablets, we said, "We will not bring in a stranger." They said, "We will bring someone in." We remained stuck in these positions 10 days, then they went to the colony and they said, "We will bring in the representatives of our father." ... tablets ... ... he will pay. Also, they did not deposit anything apart from one talent of silver from the assets tied up in short term credit and those with Anatolians and smuggled goods of their merchants. With regard to the goods which came up from the City, we checked his brothers or partners, and they deposited 9 12 talents tin and 150 textiles. We said, "Where are the letters which you brought from the City" They said, "We sent them to him." They destroyed the copies. Regarding the wool that he gathered from here, there are no copies. We have released the certified tablets with the names of the merchants to his sons. ... 2 piz.. 7 house servants and the remainder ... They said, "... ."

translation: From Aššur-idī to Ilī-ālum and Aššur-taklāku; to Ilī-ālum: You know, twice you did this to me; now you have done it a third time Did you respect your lord when you did not send me the silver Travelers have come here at least twice, but you had acquired nothing and you have not sent me the 10 minas of silver. For every mina or half mina they prowl around me. Ask Usur-ša-Aššur there Please, send the rest of my silver with the caravan With respect to the 40 minas--I take divine Aššur as witness that I shall not make any concessions to you regarding interest, which runs from the month Mahhur-ili, eponymy Iddin-Aššur, the son of Kūbī-idī. Clear the goods from your own caravan, set out and come here. Also, Aššur-taklāku must clear his goods, set out and come here --before harvest.

translation: From Aššur-idī to Aššur-nādā and Ilī-ālum: When you were about to leave I said to you: "When I have cleared myself of obligations, I shall write to you.'" I have now cleared myself, and the words of the gods are urgent. Please, the very day you hear this letter you must offer for sale the houses, both of your slave-girls and both of the grinding-girls, and then send me the silver Then you must rent a house and settle there. Further, should there be no purchaser, you must still leave the house. Indeed, you must rent a house and settle there Please, please, pay heed to the words of the letter Sell everything If you have not sold everything--as the words of the gods are urgent--you will perish Do strive to give me every mina of silver and send word to me as soon as possible. Also, send my servant to the house of ... Bread ... for ... we shall return to you, and Karriya's son who has paid 1 mina of silver. My god is the owner of the silver.

translation: From Aššur-idī to Aššur-nādā, Ilī-ālum and Aššur-taklāku: Alulaya's son owes me 12 minas of silver. Seize him and make him pay the silver. If he is absent, then write to him by means of one of my servants to where he is staying, so he can make him pay the silver. If his term for repayment is not up yet, then have him seal the silver in accordance with his contract. Let him send it to his representatives and to me, so we can purchase goods for him.

translation: From Aššur-idī to Aššur-nādā: Why have you written me as follows: "Alāhum's son will seize some of your silver" To whom do I owe anything, since it was our agreement that Šū-Aššur will place 2 talents of tin under the seal of the City authorities, before you and you will choose one of the two and pay 10 minas of silver promptly. Moreover, that very tablet Šū-Aššur brought you personally Why should he seize any silver He is depriving you with words. Instead of two containers he showed you only one; moreover, that one had been opened If indeed I owe anything to his father, then let him write to his father, so that his father can seize me here. Take what tin you are able to there, and act like a gentleman and give them the silver. The matter should not be heard there.

translation: From Aššur-idī to Aššur-nādā: If you are delayed, then divide every single shekel of silver, as much as you carry, into two parts, and send me one half as soon as possible; then send the rest with the following transport. translation: Ennasu’in, der Sohn des Ikū’am und Puzurištar, der Sohn des Alâbum, sind für die Frau des Ikuppi’a, die Töchter des Ikuppī’a und die Söhne des Ikuppī’a an deren Stelle eingetreten, und haben 40 Minen Silber, die Shculd des Ikuppī’a, dem Aššurmuttabbil, dem Sohne des Pūšukēn, und dem Bēlānum, dem Kommissär des Pūšukēn, bezahlt. translation: Aššur-pilah, the attorney of the estate of Amur-Ištar, Suen-rēʾī, Il-bānī, Aššur-nīšu, and Šū-Laban, sons of Amur-Ištar on their own behalf and on behalf of Ab-šalim, daughter of Amur-Ištar and Iddin-Adad their brother, and Aššur-mutabbil, Buzāzu and Ikūppaša, sons of Pūšu-kēn on their own behalf and on behalf of Aḫaḫa their sister the gubabtum priestess and Sueyya their brother Sueyya seized us in their agreement and swore the oath of the city and concluded their case: Amur-Ištar stood as the legal representative of Pūšu-kēn. Pūšu-kēn stood as the representative of Amur-Ištar. One sent accounts to the other. Each brother accepted silver for the funds of the other. Sealed tablets with their seals or with witnesses or dividends invested in each other. Either in the city or abroad, the sons of Amur-ištar and the daughter of the Amur-Ištar, the gubabtum priestess, and the sons of Pūšu-kēn and the daughter of Pūšu-kēn, the gubabtum priestess, will not return to each other for any matter. The following men were the adjudicators on the matter: Usānum s. Amur-Aššur, Kulumay s. Aššur-imittī, Ḫuniya s. Aššur-imittī, Ṭāb-ṣilla-Aššur s. Aššur-idi, Puzur-enna s. Enna-Aššur, Aššur-taklāku s. Āl-aḫum, Bēlānum s. Šū-Aššur, Idi-Aššur s. Dān-Aššur.

translation: Siegel des Usānum, des Sohnes des Āmuraššur; Siegel des Kulumā´ā, des Sohnes des Aššurimittī; Siegel des Ḫuni’a, des Sohnes des Aššurimittī; Siegel des Tāb-ṣillaššur, des Sohnes des Aššuridī; Siegel des Aššurtaklāku des Sohnes des Alâḫum; Siegel des Bēlānum, des Sohnes des Šū’aššur; Siegel des Puzurenna, des Sohnes des Enna’aššur; Siegel des Idī’aššur, des Sohnes des Dānaššur; Siegel des Aššurpilaḫ, des Komissäars des Hauses Āmurištar; Siegel des Su’inrē’ûm, Siegel des Ilībāni, Siegel des Aššurnīsū, Siegel des Šūlaban, der Söhne des Āmurištar; Siegel des Aššurmuttabbil, Siegel des Buzāzu, Siegel des Ikuppāša, der Söhne des Pūšukēn; Aššurpilaḫ, der Kommissär des Houses Āmurištar, Su’inrē’ûm, Ilībāni, Aššurnīšu und Šūlaban, in eigener Sache und als Vertreter der Abšalim, der Tochter des Āmurištar, und des Iddinadad, ihres Bruders, Aššurmuttabbil, Buzāzu, Ikuppāša, die Söhne des Pūšukēn, in eigener Sache und als Vertreter der Aḫāḫā ihrer Schwester, der gubabtum-Priesterin, und ihres Bruders Su’e’a haben auf ihre gegenseitgigen Verpflichtungen uns als Richter genommen. Den Eid bei der Stadt haben sie geleistet. Dann haben wir ihre Rechtsstreitigkeiten beendet: Entweder ist Āmurištar als Vertreter des Pūšukēn ist als Vertreter des Āmurištar aufgetreten; oder der eine hat dem anderen ein Depôt geschickt: Entweder hat der eine des anderen Silber vom Außenstand eingenommen, oder, was eine Doppel- urkunde mit den Siegeln des einen von ihnen oder das Gut der Karawanen beziehungsweise die Vorräte betrifft, so hat der eine es dem anderen aufgespeichert, und zwar sowohl in Assur als auch in Kappadokien. Die Söhne des Āmurištar und die Tochter des Āmurištar, die gubabtum-Priesterin, die Söhne des Pūšukēn und die Tochter des Pūšukēn, die gubabtum-Priesterin: Die eine Partei wird auf die andere in irgendeiner Sache nicht zurckkommen. Diese Leute waren die Beender der Rechtssachen.

translation: To Pūšu-kēn from Aššur-mālik: You wrote me. You said, "The copper from your account has been seized." I paid to him 14 talents of tin three months ago. As for myself and Šumi-abiya, on the day that I heard your letter, the man's son paid the certified agents of the man and I said, "Your father is my agent." As for me, copper and silver as much as their are, 8 talents of fine copper, 4 minas and 45 shekels of silver, we seized and we sealed them with seal of Šumi-abiya and my seal and deposited them in my inn. He purchased merchandise worth 6 minas silver and the merchandise was seized. They sent it for its release. Now, they will go and we will seize the goods. 4 talents of fine copper is deposited in my inn at Ulama. Now, we will write to them and we will seize him.

translation: From Šalim-Aššur, Imdī-ilum, and Pūšu-kēn and Ilī-bāni to Kuziza: Ilī-bāni brought 18 minas silver under your seal. 6 shekels were lost in the washing process. We gave 1 shekels for the smith and wood. 3 23 shekels 15 grains poor quality silver under our seals is available in the house of Pūšu-kēn. Your silver was deducted 16 12 shekels both deductions and losses. Also, according to your instructions, in addition to the 18 minas silver which Ilī-bāni brought, we acquired for you 13 minas 16 12 shekels refined silver at a 1 shekel per mina per month rate and they sealed our tablet. 31 minas refined silver, your debt, we weighed out to Pūšu-kēn. We asked him about your tablet and he said, "Their terms are two weeks past due. Have them pay the interest so that I may give you his tablet. I hold your tablet for interest." Let Kuzizīya come and we will negotiate about the interest. Take care to send the 13 minas 16 12 shekels silver which we took for interest.

translation: Zu Pūšukēn sprich Folgendermaßen Kulumā’a: Auch wenn der Angestellte des Kura mit Enumaššur wegen ihrer Angelegenheiten sich irgendwie streiten sollte, mein Vater bist du, mein Herr bist du bringe meine Sachen zu Ende, soweit du kannst. 9¾ Seqel Silber, den Preis für 1 Mine 13 Seqel Zinn, das ich dem Allu gegeben habe und welches Silber Ikuppī’aššur im Hause des Ḫabu’ālā erhalten hat, dieses Silber habe ich erhalten. Zu dem Silber, das ich dem Šamaštaklāku gegeben habe, füge es hinzu; dann siegle das Silber und schicke es mir. Die ⅓ Minen 2½ Seqel Silber, den Preis für 2½ Kutānū des Dānaššur, womit du mein Konto belastet hast, kannst du von meiner Provision abziehen. Dort braucht das Silber von deinem Konto nicht abzugehen. Dein Aufzeichnung hat er mir gegeben. Das Zinn und die Stoffe des Dānaššur und die 6 Kutānū seiner Schwester sind dir sichergestellt. Den Imku’a, den Šūkūbum und die anderen Boten schicke her Mit dem ersten von ihnen wird die Ware an dich abgehen. Mein Vater bist du, mein Herr bist du Wegen meiner Angelegenheiten betreffend das Haus des Kurā sei achtsam Zu Buzāzu sprich: "⅚ Minen 5 Seqel, Blumen ‘, die ich dir,überlassen‘ habe, schicke an unseren Ennasu’in"

translation: To Pūšu-kēn from Šū-Kūbum: In accordance with the letter which you wrote to me, we gathered your investors and we brokered an agreement. Now, their sealed tablet they bring to you. 3 fine 'finished' textiles, 7 kutānum-textiles, in all 10 textiles belonging to your wife, she entrusted them to Kulumaya in my presence and he brings them to you. Aššur-taklāku your servant brings you one bundle of lapis belonging to your wife. My dear brother, you and Innāya take half of the tin and textiles in Atata's charge and in accordance with what we discussed here, send the 'corresponding' silver. Silver in the charge of PN ... fragmentary ... take. Do not disappoint me. Act in such a way that when you do me a favor, you do not disappoint me. My dear brother, take heed to deposit my share, silver, textiles, or whatever they will invest so that they balance me in the same way they balance you and do me a favor. As for the documents which states, 'Concerning the matter of Innāya,' which you brought in your transport, you and Innāya read them and when you have read them, you and Innāya seal them and entrust them to a reliable affiliated trader so that he puts them in protective casing and brings them to me. Now, take heed concerning the matter of Šū-Suen. May Aššur and DN witness that Kulumaya ... in Burallum. He did not want to receive the 10 minas to Ali-...'s representatives and ... silver ...

translation: To Pūšu-kēn from Amur-Ištar-ma: Concerning the tin belonging to Ḫinnaya about which you wrote, that affiliated trader and his packer are here. I deposited the tin belonging to the house of Aššur-mālik for copper at a rate of 15 minas and there was copper available. But then a great number of Eblaites arrived here and much copper was weighed out to them in the palace and they returned silver at 2 12 minas refined. In 10 days its copper will be exhausted. I will purchase silver and send it to you.

translation: Zu Aššurnādā sprich Folgendermaßen Aššuriddin: ½ Mine 7½ Seqel Silber ist Amurrabbāni mir schuldig. Seine Dopel-urkunde habe ich seit {dem Eponymat} fünf Jahren dir überlassen. Entweder läßt du ihn das Silber zahlen, oder meine Urkunde gibst du mir zurück. Wie ich immer wieder höre, ist Amurrubbāni nach Kaniš gekommen. Silber, 1 oder 2 Minen, ist ihm anvertraut. Mein Bruder bist du Lade ihn vor und laß ihn das Silber zahlen Wenn er sich auf dem Markte nicht zeigt, beauftrage den Schreiber des Kārum bezüglich des Hauses der Šad’a, der Tochter des Su’eddādā.

translation: To Šū-Kūbum and Aššur-pilah, and specifically to Šū-Kūbum, from Aššur-nādā: With regard to the silver with which our father has become indebted to the fund of divine Šar-mātēn, they seized me here and said: "Pay the silver, your father's debt." I answered: "You have received silver repeatedly, so little silver is left of the debt. There are memoranda of my father's available." They said: "Produce your father's memoranda and let us see." One person representing you and one stranger entered the house together with me and we opened for the tablets and took out the memoranda and I showed them; I pleaded with them ... sacrifices ... and ... we took out the memoranda and copies of the tablets from the Gate of the God concerning our own tablet ... in the copy of the certified tablet of the Gate of the God which may appear, concerning x mina 5 shekels of silver from Alāhum's debtthat Amur-Ištar paid to Aššur-re'i. Aššur-re’i said as follows to Amur-Ištar: "Your one-mina weight is too light." His one-mina weight was checked and he then paid him 1 12 shekel of silver. Witnessed by Libbaya son of Uzua, by Ennānum, the inn-keeper; Nab-Suen son of Illil-bāni was our co-witness. For this matter, the Kanesh colony gave us permission, and we gave our testimonies before the dagger of Aššur.

translation: To Abaya from Aššur-nādā: In accordance with the message I sent to you, Innaya has here discussed with the tamkāru on your behalf of you and your paternal household. He became unhappy becasue of Kura. He said,"If he is not given instructions directly from her, these people will put continual pressure on travelers in the City, and then this one will sieze lots of silver there and constantly cause my reputation harm." As for the x3 wooden beamsof your house, Kura had sold them before I arrived at Kanesh. I discussed that with you in that very place. I said, "The house of Anaḫ-Ištar is almost finished, and it is you who should ..."

translation: From Assur-nada to Ili-alum: Against the will of the god misfortune has fallen upon me, as they have just written to me in Uršu. My dear brother, act in such a way that no evildoer may do harm to our father's house While I may still be saved- 9 talents 20 minas of my copper that Aššur-taklāku has given on commission to an agent, 8 talents 40 minas less 23 mina apart from the transport tariff, which you have bought for me--- out of which you sent 5 talents to Burušhaddum, and whose proceeds I have already received- 1 talent 18 minas of good broken copper, proceeds from the sale of 3 donkeys, which you gave in commission to an agent, of that 10 minas belong to you, 25 minas of good copper, proceeds from the sale of a donkey, owed by me. The copies concerning Šalim-bēlī's earlier caravan are not here; guard the tablet with my instructions 45 kutānu-textiles and 25 minas of sealed tin, apart from what I gave to him for expenses, Šalim-bēlī brought to you earlier. 72 kutānu-textiles, 2 of those abami'u-textiles, 4 black donkeys plus their harness, 1 mina of tin and worth 2 23 shekels 15 grains of silver of small goods you carried personally. 4 kutānu-textiles are owed by Kurub-Ištar. The terms for the agent are overdue by 7 months. My dear brother, send as much silver as falls into your hands to Uśur-ša-Aššur, so he may let it reach me and I shall not be put to shame. While could still I oblige you I gave 8 shekels of silver for the fodder of 2 donkeys and 1 shekel for your porters. 2 shekels were for the share of Aššur-šamši, witnessed by Šū-Suen the son of Itūr-ilī. I bound him by contract to pay 12 mina per textile, witnessed by Aššur-tāb and Aššur-dān.

translation: Zu Puzuraššur sprich Folgendermaßen Igā’a: Was all das betrifft, worüber du klagst: Wer ist in Turḫumit, der dauernd gegen einen Großkaufmann ein Urteil fällt Als Su’e’a herkam, gab man gewöhnlich Zinn zum Kurs von je 9 Minen oder je 10 Minen. Ich habe je 11 Minen dir geschickt Aššur und die Götter der Bruderschaft mögen Zeuge sein 5 Minen Zinn von deinem Zins habe ich Ḫanānum zu einem Kurs von je 30 Minen sehr schlechtes Kupfer gegeben. Der hat es bereits weggebracht. Nicht einen einzigen Seqel von der Abgabe hat er mir gegeben. In Sachen Igmillum ärgerst du dich. Er tut doch wohl dauernd Unrechtes Ferner habe ich 55 Minen . . . . . . Kupfer, 12 Minen gutes Bruch- Kupfer 6 Minen sind Abzüge dem Šū-ištar gegeben. Das Kupfer, das Ennasu dir gebracht hat, nimm es Wegen des Kupfers der Šadunum , bezüglich dessen sie mir geschrieben hat: 6 Minen . . . . . . . . an ihren Herren hat sie weggebracht .

transliteration: a-na PUZUR4-a-šùr qí-bi4-ma um-ma il5-we-da-ku-ma a-bi4 a-ta be-li a-ta i-na u4-mì-im ša ṭup-pì ta-ša-me-ú i-hi-id-ma hu-ša-ha-kà 5 u4-me e-zi-ma a-wa-tí bu-tù-uq-ma a-na té-er-tí-ni lá-ak-nu-uš-ma ha-ra-ni le-pu-uš 1 ma-na KÙ.BABBAR lu i-a-am lu ku-a-am qá-tí ú-kà-al ITU.KAM iš-té-en6 ITU.2.KAM e ta-áš-lu-uṭ-ma a-wa-tí e lá ta-ag-mu-ur-ma e a-sí-li-ih mì-nam ma-da-tim lu-lá-pì-ta-ku-um i-na ṭup-pì ù na-áš-pè-ra-tim lu-ša-am-ṭí-kà hu-ut-kà ú-ma-kál lá i-bi-at té-er-ta-kà za-ku-tám lu-ta-e-ra-ma KÙ.BABBAR 1 ma-na lu-uš-ta-aṣ-bi-it-ma ki-ma ma-áš-kà-tám ni-ša-ku-nu-ma lá ni-ba-šu le-pu-uš 10 GÍN KÙ.KI ší-im a-ni-qí-im ša a-mu-tim ša hu-ut-kà ub-lá-ni ku-nu-ki-a hu-ut-kà na-áš-a-kum
translation: Zu Puzuraššur sprich Folgendermaßen Ilīwēdāku: Mein Vater bist du Mein Herr bist du An dem Tage, an dem du meine Tafel liest, sei achtsam Deinen Bedarf notiere innerhalb von fünf Tagen. Meine Angelegenheit erledige Dann will ich deinem Bescheid mich beugen und dementsprechend meine Reise unternehmen. 1 Mine Silber sei es nun meines oder deines, halte ich in Händen. Einen Monat oder zwei Monate sollst du nicht darüber verfügen. Denn meine Angelegenheien hast du nicht erledigt und soll ich da nicht angesteckt werden. Was soll ich dir noch viel schreiben Mit Tafeln und Briefen will ich es dir kurz machen Ḫutka soll nicht einmal übernachten; einen klaren Bescheid von dir soll er mir bringen. Das Silber, 1 Mine, will ich bereitlegen. Dann möge er, damit wir das Depot niederlegen können und nicht zuschanden werden, handeln. 10 Seqel Silber, den Preis für den Ring aus Eisen, den Ḫutka mir gebracht hat, mit meinen Siegeln: damit ist Ḫutka zu dir unterwegs.

translation: From Imdī-ilum, Enna-Bēlum and Aššur-ṣulūlī to Puzur-Aššur: From the 245 textiles and those of the transporters of the transport of Amur-Ištar, therein, 3 textiles of the Akkadian type were left in the hosue of your father-in-law in Ḫaḫḫum. They cleared the reaminder of your textiles, 92 textiles from the transport of Idi-Adad, combined with the textiles of the transporters and they are available. The son of Erraya Aššur-mālik brought his contraband into the city to Pūšu-kēn, but his contraband was seized and the palace seized Pūšu-kēn and placed him in jail. The guards are strong. The princessqueen sent to Luḫušattiya, Ḫurrama, Šalaḫšua, and her own land concerning the contraband and ENNATUm is established. Urgent, do not deal in contraband If you departed from Timelkiya, I ... you, whatever you sent out, leave it in a good house in Timelkiya and leave one of your trustworthy ṣuḫārum-servants and you yourself leav it and be counseled here. Also, if anyone tries to get you to agree for even a single shekel of silver for whatever you have, saying "Sell me tin or textiles so that I can smuggle them and I will be responsible.", do not sell There, a hand is set in hand against you.

translation: From Alāhum and Aššur-idī to Aššur-nādā and Šū-Aššur; specifically to Aššur-nādā: the same day that you hear the letter Šū-Aššur shall give you 1 talent of tin under the seal of the City, and you must pay him 10 minas of refined silver promptly. Why is it that you say: "You have seized my silver" Have I removed any of your silver in this way Deduct it from the merchandise transported by Ennam-BēIum. But you yourself, have you not sent the 15 minas that you promised me from Abum to where it pleased you As to the silver transported by Izimea and Hinnaya, their terms are overdue. Send the silver as soon as possible. With respect to the certified tablet with the testimony of Lā-qēp and Aššur-imittī son of Amur-ilī, before he leaves you must show him the tablet with his testimony and his seal with one of the travellers as witness, and then erase the words on the tablet. Please, take Alāhum's tin and scatter it among colleagues and friends and pay him his silver.

translation: To Aššur-nādā and Iddin-Suen from Ilī-ālum: Previously, before you sent me your goods, I wrote to you, saying: "Do not send any goods to me" CHECK TRANSLATION: You drive them verily yourself, so that I do not clear any of my own things. As your goods arrived, I cleared copper worth 10 or 15 minas of silver for Aššur-taklāku, and kept it back on account of your goods. Further, I shall make at least 20 talents of copper or more for you. I Also, x minas you received from my outstanding claims and thus opened my eyes. You must write to me soon about Šarmama and his partners. His son is dead. We were unable to go to him. You will write to me later. During the sikkātum it is not feasible for us to live up to the promises with respect to your outstanding claims. The accounting concerning Abum-ilī's enterprise has not taken place. I asked Turaya, who said: "I balanced 12 shekels of silver for Iddin-Suen." Twice I have written to you. Within 3 months after they have paid the balance and the price of the textiles has been received, Abum-ilum must pay the balance to you. If he does not pay, he must add interest for me. Why has he not paid in accordance with his contract Indeed, Iddin-Suen will receive 12 shekels from Turaya. Your 5 talents of copper Šalim-beli has brought into Burušhaddum.

translation: To Pūšu-kēn from Ilabrat-bāni: Concerning the missive about which you wrote, you said, "Let me write a tablet to your representatives so that they give me the tablets infrom the city." Should I not depart with Ikūn-pī-Aššur, and the son of Ennamānum returne to take the silver, then I will take the tablet of my transport. Also then, depart to Šalatuwar and I will take the tablet of my transport and I set out and depart. At my arrival open so that Ihe write a tablet to you and give me the tablets. translation: Seals: Bezīya s. Anaḫ-ilī, Ilī-rēʾī s. Šū-Kūbum, Aššur-bani s. Kurbāya. Aššur-bāni owes 4 minas refined silver. He will add 1 12 shekels per mina per month as interest from the month of Kuzallu, eponymate of Ṣilūlu. Seals: Šū-Laban s. Dān-ilī, Bezīya s. Anaḫ-ilī, Nimar-Adad s. Enna-Suen, Amur-Ištar s. Išar-kit-Ištar. Amur-Ištar received 4 minas silver, the price of the housesmy house. Seals: Lipit-Ištar, Ṭāb-Aššur s. Enlil-bāni, Kuzīya s. Buzizi, Imlikaya. Imlikaya owes 2 minas 41 13 shekels refined silver. He will add 1 12 shekels per mina per month as interest from the month of Qarrātum, eponymate of Ṣilūlu. Seals: Aššur-bāni s. Kurbāya, Ilī-rēʾī s. Šū-Kūbum, Imlikaya. Imlikaya owes 3 minas silver. He will add 1 12 shekels per mina per month as interest from the month of Qarrātum, eponymate of Ṣilūlu. Seals: Iluku s. Šū-Ištar, Ištar-bāni s. Asquidim. Ištar-bāni owes 18 shekels refined silver. Month: Kuzallu. Eponymate: Buzuzu. Seals: Uṣur-ša-Aššur s. Agua, Aššur-mālik s. Puzur-Ištar, Puzur-Aššur. Aššur-mālik owes 3 minas refined silver. Month: Ṣipʾum. Eponymate: Aššur-damiq. Seals: Abu-šalim s. Asqūdum, Takil-Aššur s. Ennānum. Takil-Aššur s. Ennānum owes 5 talents 15 minas poor quality copper. They will add 1 12 minas per talent per month as interest from the month of Qarrātum, eponymate of Ilī-dān. Seals: Šalim-Aššur s. Ipḫurum, Atata s. Akutum, Ilī-ašranni s. Šū-Bēlum. Suen-pilaḫ s. Šū-Bēlum owes the merchant 11 minas refined silver. He will add 1 12 shekel per mina per month as interest from the month of Ab šarrānē, eponymate after Ilī-dān. Seals: Idī-ilum s. Šar-ilī, Abiya s. Aššur-imittī, Abu-šalim s. Asqūdum. Abu-šalim s. Asqūdum owes 3 minas refined silver. He will pay 30 shekels in one year. If he does not pay on time, he will add 1 12 shekels per mina per month as interest. Month: Allānātum. Eponymate: Buzutaya. Seperately, 1 mina silver is his beʾulātum loan. Seals: Aššur-bāni s. Kurubāya, Suen-pilaḫ s. Šū-Bēlum, Kuzīya s, Buzizi. Aššur-bāni s. Kurbāya owes 2 minas 6 shekels refined silver. He will add 1 12 shekels per mina per month as interest from the month of Ša kēnātim, eponymate after Ṣilūlu. Seals: Mannum-bālum-Aššur, Kudātum, Aššur-imittī, Aššur-mālik. Al-abum owes 33 shekels silver. Guarantor: Kudātum. He will pay after he returns to the City.

translation: To Pūšu-kēn from Tariš-mātum and Ištar-lamassī: Our dear father and lord, none of the youth should ask you for silver, and you must not release silver to their accounts. We depend on you We paid out 2 minas silver for the plot of Idī-Ištar. We have heard nothing about Uṣur-ša-Aššur We have shipped off all your merchandise. Our dear father, decide wherever you can salvage his capital. It is sent to his father. Decide how much capital you can salvage.

translation: To Pūšu-kēn from Lamassī: When you were staying here, I gave 1 heavy textile to Aššur-mālik. Also, when he returned, I gave to him 1 kamtum textile and 3 kutānum-textiles. Why is it that the textiles which I keep sending to you, which he is supposed to bring, he does not bring to you Let your message come and so inform me. Also, concerning the textiles about which you wrote, you said, "They are too small. They are no good" Was it not according to your request that I made them smaller Also, when you wrote me, you said, "Raise a 12 mina each for your textiles." I raised it. Also, Urāni did settle the logs to your representative, concerning the beams he confirmed. I did not exhaust it. Also, he took the beams belonging to your brother. The copper which you gave to him for the beams he did not give at all. Ilī-bāni brought to the youth a namšuḫam-textile belonging to Aḫaḫa. Later, I will send a nibrarum-textile to him.

translation: From Aššur-idī to Aššur-nādā: You sent me 2 minas less 12 shekel of silver with Ištar-pilah. I took 1 mina 12 shekel out of what belongs to Šū-Ištar. In all: 3 minas of silver. Thereof I paid 7 12 shekels as import duty; since the money for the transport tariff had been spent, I paid the balance of 1 shekel of silver. The rest of your silver amounts to 2 56 minas 1 12 shekel. I borrowed 8 shekels of silver from the son of Abu-šalim and his partner. I still had a claim against you of 2 23 minas 1 14 shekels of silver, the proceeds from the sale of the textiles transported by Ennam-Bēlum. You said: ''The silver has been taken." But I forgot to seal it, and since I have no silver available to me I have taken it. I also still had a claim of 16 shekels 15 grains of silver from the goods transported by the son of Irnuid. In all: 2 56 minas 7 13 shekels have been deducted, so the rest of your silver is 2 16 shekels. It has been spent for you.

translation: From Aššur-idī to Aššur-nādā: Concerning Iddin-Suen about whom you wrote, I seized Iddin-Suen and in the presence of our colleagues I said: "You have taken silver from my outstanding claims Give me my silver" He answered: "I have not taken any of your silver." So, he cheated me with the account, for he has taken at least 1 or 2 minas of silver at my expense. "Reckoned from the month Tanbarta in the eponymy of Ibni-Adad son of Baqqunum he is to pay 1 mina per year He carries goods worth at least 1 or 2 minas of silver. Seize him there and act as a gentleman. Please, free yourself of claims, set out and come at harvest time together with Aššur-malik. If you have taken tin as an investment loan, then give it in commission to agents on fixed terms. Please, send me Ilī-ālum with the first travelers.

translation: From Aššur-idī to Aššur-nādā: You left me 3 23 minas of silver; 1 mina 12 shekel of silver belongs to Šū-Ištar; 2 minas less 12 shekel of silver you sent to me with Ištar-pilah; Dān-Aššur brought me 1 13 mina of refined silver--in all: 8 minas. Thereof I sent off to you goods worth 2 minas 16 23 shekels less 7 12 grains with Aššur-nādā son of Irnuid; I further gave him 2 14 shekels, the wages of a donkey-driver. 16 12 shekels of silver to Šū-Suen and 4 12 shekels to Asqūdia-- I gave to them, they are bound by contract. If they have no claims on you, they must repay you in tin at the rate 16: 1. Also Aššur-rē'ī has been bound by contract at the rate 16:1 in tin for your remaining claim on him. Seize him to have him pay. After the price of the copper and 1 shekel 15 grains of silver, which he owed to you, had been paid, I paid as balance to Aššur-rē'ī 23 shekels 22 12 grains of silver. 13 mina of silver, the price of a donkey, I paid to Uṣur-ša-Aššur. The day you left you took 5 minas of scrap metal worth 4 shekels of silver. The export duty was 12 shekel 15 grains; you wrote me about it, and I added it. As to the 5 12 minas of silver carried by Ennam-Aššur, 3 shekels were found to be missing during the check, but I forgot to charge it to you at the accounting. 2 sheep belonging to Pidaya's son: 5 12 mina; 1 sheep worth 1 56 mina belonging to Iddin-ilum; 1 sheep: 3 minas, 1 sheep 2 13 minas 5 shekels, 1 sheep: 2 minas 10 shekels belonging to Aššur-rē'ī; 1 sheep worth 2 13 minas belonging to Zua; 1 sheep worth 2 23 minas belonging to Dunnia; 1 sheep worth 3 13 minas--the same Dunnia's eldest son. You forgot 1 textile worth 8 23 minas belonging to Aššur-ṭab, so I paid. The total in copper: 32 minas less 5 shekels, in silver: 13 mina less 56 shekels, I have paid as the price of the textile and the sheep which you forgot about. I paid as compensation 1 x shekels after the transport tariff on your silver transported by Bēlī-ālum and the son of the priest. After the transport tariff had been spent I paid as compensation 3 less 14 shekels of silver to Ištar-pilah and Irnuid's son. 1 mina of silver I spent on the price of 2 oxen and grain to feed the sons. The rest of your silver: 2 minas 23 shekels, I deducted from the 5 minas 1 shekel of silver, the shipment transported by Ennam-Bēlum; send the rest of my silver, 2 minas 13 shekels as soon as possible. Do not be angry. I wanted it for the men, so I took it.

translation: From Aššur-idī to Aššur-nādā and Aššur-taklāku: to Aššur-nādā: You have sent me 12 mina of silver from your votive offerings for divine Aššur. They are bringing to you 4 kutānu-textiles. I gave 3 shekels for his expenses. Let him establish the tin for you at the same rate they use for others. Šū-Nūnu brings it to you. To Aššur-taklāku: You sent me 12 mina 5 shekels of silver from your votive offerings to divine Aššur. I have deducted its import duty and .... and the rest of the silver break .... Clear it and send the silver to me with the first traveler. To Aššur-taklāku: If you are truly my brother, clear the remainder of the goods transported by you and send it to me, and let it be shipped even while you are delayed so every shekel of silver is active for me. I wrote you about the later shipment I sent to you, saying: "I have to pay the money to the City Hall." Take care and send me the silver.

translation: From Buzutaya, Ennum-Bēlum and Puzur-Aššur to Pūšu-kēn: After we sent the silver from the cargo of Ilī-bāni, Tarmana gave us 2 minas 45 shekels silver. Dalaš gave to us 1 mina silver. Aššur-ṭāb took 4 shekels. There are 8 shekels of poor quality silver. 7 shekels are deductions. The remainder of the silver is 5 minas 26 shekels. From the 2 minas 31 shekels of your silver about which there is agreeing, they deducted from us 1 mina 6 shekels on account of Puzur-Aššur. Let it be released there with you. We took the remainder of the silver, 1 minas 24 shekels. Altogether 4 minas 50 shekels. We weighed out 3 minas 16 shekels for 21-ma. Thereof, the remainder of the silver is 1 minas 34 shekels. Also, Puzur-Aššur gave us 1 minas 13 12 shekels silver and concerning 2 minas 37 shekels silver which was in Il-bāni's cargo for the filling of the sack, he said, "That which we took for you on interest, we will weigh out the silver and its interest."

translation: From Šū-Ḫubur to Pūšu-kēn and Ennum-Aššur: To Ennam-Aššur: I hear that my representatives entrusted to you 10 minas silver credit from my goods there. If you are my brother and though your terms remain 1 or two months more, pay the silver and send it to me. Do me this favor. I am a man of favors.
